- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is negative (e.g., -0.43 or lower) — model tends to overshoot upward.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative and recent prices are trending down — model fails to recognize mean reversion.
- When sentiment turns from negative to neutral/positive, model often overreacts with a sharp upward bias — adjust downward slightly.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile — reduce initial forecast by 0.5–1.5% for volatile sentiment periods.
- If last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, model tends to overfit that trend — cap forecast increase at 1.5% above recent peak.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., -0.5+), model underestimates true price rise — add 0.8–1.2% to forecast to account for sentiment-driven rebound.
- Avoid extrapolating from 18-day history — model overfits short-term trends; use 30-day moving average as baseline for correction.
